# The Engine 14 example slate: keep, renew, retire or new, per group

## Context

The operator, Mon 16 Nov 2026 (relayed): what matters a lot is which examples Engine 14 shows. It needs many new ones, some existing ones are old, and the grids need more. A leaf of #21140, for the cut on Mon 23 Nov.

## The Problem

Nobody has decided, example by example, what the section shows. [The inventory](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20498#issuecomment-6918253093) counts 139 runnable examples and 15 apps; the catalog publishes 72. The leaves so far add records and covers for whatever exists. Two readers without session context named what that produces ([the first look](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21130#issuecomment-6918809237)): tiles that read as toys (a lorem-ipsum tree, a cube, a clock, an empty calendar) and thin groups (Scheduler 1, Gantt 1, Calendar 2, Tree 2).

Discussion #20742 asked the same on 10 Nov (its OQ4 and OQ5) and proposed a bar: an example can be reset and inspected at desktop and phone width, in the supported themes, by keyboard; a new demonstration names the visitor's question and shows why no existing example answers it. Neither was filed.

## The Architectural Reality

- `examples/**` and `apps/**` on dev; `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` (77 records; `feature`, `lookFor`, `scope`).
- The six inventory sheets under `review-evidence/20498/inventory-2026-11-16/` at commit `53e279b1d0` (branch `clio/20498-first-screen-look`).
- Design authority: the operator's direction of 16 Nov on #20498; the publication bar of Discussion #20742.

## The Fix

One table on this ticket, grids first, a row per runnable entry:

- **keep**, **renew** (what changes: the data, the default state, the theme, the size) or **retire** from the catalog, with one reason;
- per group, the **new** examples Engine 14 needs: the question each answers, and why no existing example can.

Every renew and every new row is then filed as its own leaf under #21140, with an owner or a curated label. The operator gets the per-group summary as one page.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every runnable entry of the inventory has a verdict and a reason.
- [ ] Every group names its new examples, or says that it needs none and why.
- [ ] Each example that stays published meets the bar, or its row says which part it fails and which leaf repairs it.
- [ ] Grid & Table, Tree, Calendar, Scheduler and Gantt each say how a visitor sees depth, not one demonstration.
- [ ] No row names a commercial feature (the rule of #20498, until 1 Dec).
- [ ] Every renew and new row links its filed leaf.
- [ ] The summary is with the operator; his objections changed rows or are answered on this ticket.

This ticket closes by comment with the table and the list of filed leaves. No pull request resolves it.

## Out of Scope

Building any example; covers; the group list itself (map v2); the workbench (its own leaf).

## Avoided Traps

- **A field-type checklist as a ticket batch.** Discussion #20742 ruled it out: a missing folder is not a missing proof.
- **A verdict from one still frame.** A row that retires or renews an example opens it first.
- **New examples to fill a count.** The count follows the questions.

## Related

Parent #21140 · Discussion #20742 (OQ4, OQ5) · #20874 (the planning families' examples) · #21039 (the timeline example, merged 16 Nov).

**What the facts say, before any example is opened**

1. **The old half is the tables.** Four entries from 2019 and 2020; the grid entries are from 2022 on, eleven of them from 2025 and 2026. Three demonstrations exist twice, once per family: COVID, cell editing, nested record fields.
2. **Leads for new grid examples** (a search for config words in the grid and table examples; a lead, not a finding, since a default needs no config):
   - of 14 built-in column types (the base class aside), 9 appear in no example: `currency`, `animatedCurrency`, `sparkline`, `icon`, `iconLink`, `countryFlag`, `githubUser`, `githubOrgs`, `linkedin`;
   - no example configures a paging toolbar, a footer toolbar, column resizing or a row drag;
   - filtering is shown once, in a table from 2020.
3. **67 entries stand on the configuration viewport.** Their verdict depends on the workbench (#21143) more than on each example.
4. **Depth is missing where the operator named it:** Calendar 2 (from 2020 and 2021), Tree 2 without a record, Scheduler, Gantt and Timeline 1 each, Board none yet (#20875).
5. **From Euclid's intake run on #21147, as inputs to the rows:** Gallery's module request failed once in Dev mode; the dialog's production URL rendered Portal chrome; an OffscreenCanvas control raised an error before the canvas was ready. The render sweep's three error leads stand: `apps/legit`, `component/wrapper/googleMaps`, `dashboard/crossWindowWitness`.

**Next (mine):** the Grid & Table rows with a verdict and a reason each, every example opened, and the per-group summary, by Tue 17 Nov, 12:00 CET.

### Retire

The record leaves the catalog. The folder stays wherever specs load it.

| Entry | Reason |
|---|---|
| `grid/lockedColumns` | A test fixture by its own source ("chosen for test math, never demo aesthetics", page title "Locked-Column Grid Fixture"). 14 spec files drive it, and its 14 year columns are empty by design. The lock itself works. New example 1 takes its place. |
| `table/covid` | The table twin of `grid/covid`: same data, same frame. |
| `table/cellEditing` | The twin, and its Country column renders empty. |
| `table/nestedRecordFields` | The twin. |
| `tablePerformance` | A bench from 2019: three tables of "Column3 - 0" cells that flash red. |
| `tableStore` | The six names and three buttons. Every other card shows sorting and store updates. |
| `serverside/gridContainer` | An empty box and a button, then the six names. The JSON it is about never appears. A lead for Workers & Platform. |

Leaf: #21186 removes six of these records. `grid/lockedColumns` keeps its record, `grid-locked-columns`, which #21167 points at the new example.

### New

Each names the visitor's question, what the engine has on dev, and why no entry can answer it.

| # | Example | The question | On dev | Why no entry answers it | Leaf |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pinned columns | Can columns stay put on the left and right while the rest scrolls? | `locked: 'start'` and `'end'` on a column | The only user is the fixture above. | #21167 |
| 2 | A filter row on the grid | Can users filter 100,000 rows per column? | `showHeaderFilters` (`src/grid/Container.mjs:221`) | The only filter row is on the table. | #21168 |
| 3 | Cell types on one sheet | What can a cell be? | 14 built-in column types under `src/grid/column/` | Seven are used by no example or app in this repository (`countryFlag`, `currency`, `githubOrgs`, `githubUser`, `icon`, `iconLink`, `linkedin`), and no example uses more than five. | #21187 |
| 4 | Export | Can the data leave the grid? | `toCsv()` and `exportCsv()` (`src/grid/Container.mjs:1915`, `:1954`) | No example or app calls either. | #21188 |
| 5 | Server-side data | How does it page, sort and filter against an API? | `pageSize`, `remoteSort`, `remoteFilter` (`src/data/Store.mjs:219` to `:250`) | `toolbar/paging` calls a backend no static host has and opens as an empty table. A mock backend is this leaf's prerequisite, as the gate of 7 Nov says. | #21189 |
| 6 | A streamed load | What does a user see while 50,000 rows arrive? | `src/data/parser/Stream.mjs`, the footer toolbar's `onStoreProgress`, the Streaming guide | No example or app here uses either. | #21190 |

Cross-listed once its own row passes: `apps/finance` (live prices in animated currency cells), which opens with half the screen empty.

**How a visitor sees depth.** The tab reads in the order of a buyer's questions: does it look like a product (the issues grid), does it scale (big data, the tree at scale), can people work in it (two ways to edit, two filter rows, selection by keyboard), can it be shaped (grouped headers, pinned columns, cell types, row heights, banding, animated sort), does it reach a backend (server-side data, a streamed load, export), and what the table is for.

**Order for the build**, the first six for the read of Fri 20 Nov: renew 1 to 4, new 1 and 2. Then renew 5 to 7 and new 3 and 4. Then the rest.

**A method note for the next sweep.** Served from a nested path, four entries show an empty Country column, because their `countries.json` URL climbs out of the tree. From the server root only `table/cellEditing` does. My first pass ran nested and read all four as broken.

**Not decided here:** the 133 entries of the other groups (Wed 18 Nov) and the per-group summary (Tue 17 Nov, 12:00 CET). The leaves for these 19 rows are filed under #21175, the group's epic.

* fix(toolbar): a breadcrumb's separators take the tertiary text color its crumbs use (#21447)

The chevron between two crumbs used --button-text-color, the text color
of filled buttons: black on neo-dark's toolbar and white on the light
ones, so a reader barely saw where one crumb ended. The crumbs are
tertiary buttons, so the separator takes --button-tertiary-text-color.

* feat(build): a capture recipe's click can name its button (#21447)

A context menu's cover needs a right-click, which the recipe vocabulary
had no step for. A click step takes button: left or right; validation
refuses any other value and any other action that names one.

* feat(examples): Buttons, Menus & Toolbars shows a context menu, a breadcrumb and a paging toolbar (#21447)

Two cards with covers taken after their content is drawn: the project
files with a context menu open at the pointer, and the breadcrumb three
levels down the engine's folders. grid-server-side joins the group
through alsoIn, which shows Neo.toolbar.Paging on the simulated server

* fix(menu): items that replace a menu's items rebuild their submenus (#21447)

Neo.menu.List caches a submenu per item key and builds it once from that
item's nested items. Items that replaced the menu's items and reused a
key, as the file list's Move to does on every right-click, reopened the
submenu of the old item, whose handlers acted on the file right-clicked
before. afterSetItems() now hides and destroys the cached submenus, and
destroy() shares the helper. A unit spec replays the two right-clicks.

* fix(build): a tile in a declared capture family needs no card recipe (#21454)

validateCaptureRecipes() asked every covered record of a declared family for
a recipe. Tiles (#21418) take their crop from the manifest's tiles list, so
declaring lists here made list-base, chip-list and color-list fail the
validation once dev's tiles met this branch. The rule now skips
kind: 'component'; a card beside a tile still needs its recipe.

Units: CaptureExamples and the Portal examples catalog, 63 passed; the new
arm fails on the old rule.

(cherry picked from commit d9c6255a49a8f526e4af9a3730de2b6e74d17bd6)

* fix(build): a tile in a declared capture family needs no card recipe (#21454)

validateCaptureRecipes() asked every covered record of a declared family for
a recipe. Tiles (#21418) take their crop from the manifest's tiles list, so
declaring lists here made list-base, chip-list and color-list fail the
validation once dev's tiles met this branch. The rule now skips
kind: 'component'; a card beside a tile still needs its recipe.

Units: CaptureExamples and the Portal examples catalog, 63 passed; the new
arm fails on the old rule.

* feat(examples): the markdown example streams on open, process and splitter get content, five records leave the catalog (#21474)

The markdown example starts its stream demo on its first mount, so the
page shows its proof without a click. The process example tells a trip
in four English stages instead of German headings over lorem ipsum, and
the splitter's panels hold a folder list and an inbox. Process and
splitter become component tiles; the markdown record gets its cover
path. The four MWC records and the real-world process form leave
examples.json, as #21142's rows decided; their folders stay.

* fix(markdown): a streamed document ends as its one-shot parse (#21477)

The example's stream demo cut "Why transcripts need this" into a heading
and a paragraph, and drew its table without a head. Three faults in the
parser's streaming path:

- A heading or break always settled, even while its line was still
  arriving. It now stays open until its line ends.
- The empty string after a final newline counted as a blank line, so a
  paragraph, list, quote or table that ended in a newline settled before
  its next line arrived, and a table header never met its delimiter. A
  block that reaches it now stays open, and its source keeps the newline
  the next append continues.
- A tail that turned into another block type kept its id, and child ids
  were numbered in creation order, so a re-parse gave one node's id to a
  node of another kind: the differ kept the paragraph's text where the
  table head belonged. A tail of a new type is now a new block, and a
  child id carries its node's kind.

A new spec streams a document with every block type in chunks of 1 to
24 characters: it ends in the same blocks as one parse, and no id names
two kinds of node. All seven arms fail on dev's parser. The promotion
spec now expects the table under a fresh id.

* feat(examples): More components declares its captures: the markdown card and the process and splitter tiles (#21474)

components joins the declared capture families with one card recipe:
the end of the document the markdown page streams on open, its table
under a head and its hostile HTML rendered as text. Process and
splitter join the tile list. The process example opens horizontal, so
its tile shows the trip's four stages in a row.

The count pins follow examples.json: 111 records, 100 live (99 in Dev
mode), More components 12 of its own, 2 cards and 10 tiles. The tile
spec hides the markdown card in Dev mode in its fixture, so its "one
kind heads neither" arm keeps a page of tiles alone. seo.json is
regenerated for the three new routes.

* fix(examples): the markdown toolbar wraps and the splitter fits a phone's stage (#21474)

* docs(examples): the markdown, process and splitter pages as released and as changed, for review (#21474)

* chore(examples): drop the review frames; they stay at 5f5706d9f1 (#21474)

* test(portal): the catalog identity test names the 112 records it loads (#21474)

The title kept a count from before this branch folded five records into
tiles; a clean merge then carried dev's 117 into it.

* fix(examples): the splitter's panes and the trip log's heading fit a phone stage, styled from their sheets (#21474)

The splitter's border, width cap and pane padding move from inline styles
into its stylesheet, which also caps the panes at the stage's height: at
390 x 844 each pane scrolls its text instead of running past the stage.

The trip log's container and heading take their styles from a new
stylesheet. Below 600px the heading shrinks, so the first stage of the
trip shows in the phone's 210px stage. At desktop widths both examples
render as before: the process and splitter tiles recapture to the bytes
neomjs/pages#133 serves.

* docs(examples): review frames of More components part 1, round 2 (#21474)

* chore(examples): drop the round-2 review frames; they stay at 9e5575dc02 (#21474)

* test(portal): the catalog spec's count table lists one group per line (#21520)

The table packed four or five groups per line, so examples PRs on
different groups edited the same or an adjacent line and conflicted:
98 of the 210 cross-group pairs, measured by merging throwaway commits
that each bump one group. One group per line leaves the 20 pairs of
neighbouring groups. Values and order are unchanged; the keys pad to
'multi-window' for check-block-alignment."
